principles.title: Principles
principles.summary: Four brand principles that every screen follows.
rules: Clear over clever: labels describe outcomes. No icon-only actions for moving money.
Honest numbers: amounts, fees and rates are never hidden or styled down. Fees use the same text size as the amount they belong to.
Calm confidence: restrained motion, generous spacing, red only for real errors.
Accessible by default: WCAG 2.2 AA minimum, APCA reported, 44px touch targets.

tokens.title: Tokens
tokens.summary: Style only with semantic CSS variables. Primitives do not exist in CSS.
rules: Use var(--lw-*) semantic tokens for every color, space, radius, size, type and motion value.
Never write hex, rgb, hsl or oklch values in components or screens.
Never reference primitive names such as --lw-color-iris-600 or --lw-space-4. They are not emitted and lint rejects them.
Spacing: --lw-space-3xs (2px), 2xs (4), xs (8), sm (12), md (16), lg (24), xl (32), 2xl (48), 3xl (64).
Radius: --lw-radius-control for inputs and buttons, --lw-radius-card for cards and dialogs, --lw-radius-pill for chips and badges.
If a token is missing, propose one. Do not hardcode.
tokens.example: .panel { padding: var(--lw-space-lg); background: var(--lw-color-surface-raised); border-radius: var(--lw-radius-card); box-shadow: var(--lw-shadow-1); }

color.title: Color
color.summary: Ink for text, Iris for actions, Teal for money in, Coral for decoration only.
rules: Text: --lw-color-text-primary, -secondary, -tertiary. All pass AA on every surface in both themes.
Surfaces: --lw-color-bg-canvas behind everything, -surface-default, -surface-raised for cards, -surface-overlay for dialogs.
Actions use --lw-color-action-* tokens. Use the Button component rather than styling buttons.
Danger red is for real errors and irreversible actions only.
Coral (--lw-color-accent-decorative) is decorative: never text, never the only signal of state, under about 10% of a screen.
State is never carried by color alone. Pair it with an icon and words.

typography.title: Typography
typography.summary: Inter with optical sizing. Type roles, not raw sizes.
rules: Use Heading (level is required) and Text components, or --lw-type-<role>-* tokens.
Roles: display lg/md, heading xl/lg/md/sm/xs, body md/sm, label md/sm, caption, amount lg/md/sm.
Minimum visible text size is 12px (caption).
Every number in an amount, balance or table column uses tabular figures.
One h1 per screen. Do not skip heading levels.

amounts.title: Amounts and money
amounts.summary: Always use AmountDisplay. Direction by sign, never by red.
rules: Render every amount with <AmountDisplay> or formatAmount(). Never format money by hand.
Incoming: plus sign and teal. Outgoing: typographic minus and ink. Outgoing is never red.
Pending money shows a clock icon and the word Pending.
tr-TR with TRY shows ₺1.250,00. en-US with TRY shows TRY 1,250.00.
Show fees next to the amount, at the same text size.
Balances can be hidden. Use BalanceHeader, which includes the toggle.
IBANs are masked on cards (maskIban) and grouped in fours when shown in full (formatIban).

forms.title: Forms
forms.summary: Visible labels, hints before, errors after, never placeholders as labels.
rules: Every input has a visible label: TextField, Select, Checkbox, RadioGroup, Switch and OTPInput all require one.
Use hint for format help before typing. Use error for what went wrong and how to fix it.
Amount fields: <TextField label="Amount" prefix="₺" inputMode="decimal" numeric />.
One-time codes: <OTPInput>. Never split a code into several inputs.
Use Switch only for settings that apply immediately. Use Checkbox inside forms.
Do not disable the submit button to hide errors.

errors.title: Errors and feedback
errors.summary: Say what happened and what to do. Calm, specific, never blaming.
rules: Write: what happened, then what to do. "This IBAN is too short. Check it and try again."
Field errors go next to the field (error prop). Not in a toast.
Toasts confirm completed actions. Danger toasts stay until dismissed.
Use Badge tones for status: neutral, info, success, warning, danger. They include an icon.
When nothing left the account, say so: "Nothing left your account."

layout.title: Layout
layout.summary: Mobile first, 4px grid, one primary action per screen.
rules: Spacing comes from --lw-space-* only. Stack sections with --lw-space-lg, related items with --lw-space-sm.
Mobile screens: max width about 440px, side padding --lw-space-md.
One primary Button per screen or section. Put the final action full width at the bottom on mobile.
Touch targets are at least 44 by 44px. Components already guarantee this.
Use Card for grouping, List with ListItem or TransactionRow for rows.

copy.title: Copy
copy.summary: Short, direct, second person. No jargon, no em dashes.
rules: Use "you". Say what happens: "Your money arrives in seconds", not "Transfer request is being processed".
Never use em dashes. Use commas, colons or periods.
No hype words: revolutionary, seamless, magic.
Button labels are verbs with an outcome: "Send ₺250", "Freeze card".
Dialog titles are questions: "Freeze your card?".

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.summary: WCAG 2.2 AA is the floor. The components do most of the work if you use them.
rules: Every interactive element is reachable by keyboard, has a visible focus ring and an accessible name.
IconButton requires label. Icon is hidden unless it has a label.
Never use color alone to carry meaning.
Use semantic elements: headings in order, lists for rows, buttons for actions, links for navigation.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion. The global styles already shorten animations.
Mark loading regions with role="status" and aria-busy while Skeletons show.

motion.title: Motion
motion.summary: Short and calm. Motion explains, it does not decorate.
rules: Durations: --lw-motion-duration-instant (100ms), fast (150), base (200), slow (300).
Easing: --lw-motion-easing-standard, -enter for elements arriving, -exit for leaving.
No looping animation except loading indicators.

dark-mode.title: Themes and dark mode
dark-mode.summary: Themes swap semantic tokens. Components never change.
rules: Set data-theme="light", "dark" or "auto" on a container. Two themes can sit side by side.
Never write theme-specific CSS in components. If something looks wrong in dark, the token mapping changes.
Dark surfaces get lighter as they rise: canvas, default, raised, overlay.

I've built `TransferScreen.tsx`, a single component with a default export. It follows the four steps you asked for and ends on a receipt with a "Money sent" toast. Every component, color and spacing value comes from the Leeward design system. The Leeward validator returned no issues, but it checked a hand-made condensed copy of the file, not the file itself. I also haven't compiled or run it: shell commands needed approval, so there's no type-check either.

**How it works**
- **Recipient:** pick one of 4 saved people or "Someone new". For a new person you enter a full name and an IBAN. The IBAN is checked for length, the TR prefix and its check digits, and it can't be your own account. Errors appear next to the field and focus moves to the first one that needs fixing.
- **Amount:** you can type Turkish-style amounts like `1.250,50`. Money is stored in whole kuruş so rounding can't drift. The screen checks the minimum (₺1), your balance including the fee, and your daily limit. The fee is shown at the same size as the amount: free to Leeward accounts, ₺6,50 to other banks.
- **Review:** shows the recipient, their bank, the full IBAN grouped in fours, amount, fee and total from your account. The button reads "Send ₺1.250,00".
- **Code:** a 6-digit code with a 3-minute expiry, a 30-second wait before resending and 3 tries. The code stays in the box after a wrong try so you can fix one digit. Holding a lock during submit stops a double send if the code auto-submits while you also press the button. Every failure message ends with "Nothing left your account."
- **Accessibility:** focus moves to the new heading at each step, there's one h1 per screen, and the back button has a label. Unfinished requests are cancelled if you leave the screen.

**Mock data**
- The test code is `123456`.
- The mock IBANs are generated by a small helper in the file so they pass the check-digit test. That helper is for mock data only.

**Things to check**
1. **Helper signatures are my guess.** The Leeward tools don't document `formatAmount`, `formatIban` or `maskIban`. I called `formatAmount(value, currency, locale)` and the other two with just the IBAN. If the real ones differ, only the `money()` helper and a few call sites need changing.
2. **App setup is assumed.** The screen expects your app root to load the Leeward fonts and styles, set `data-theme`, and wrap everything in `ToastProvider` and `TooltipProvider`. Without `ToastProvider`, the toast call will fail.
3. **The saved-recipient list stops at 5 options.** It uses a radio group, which Leeward caps at about 5 choices (4 saved people plus "Someone new"). A longer list would need a searchable list instead.
4. **New-recipient names must have two parts.** A single-word name is rejected, which suits personal transfers but not company names.
